clue.text: Excellent recommendation for better cover

parts.note: a better is one who bets, and a racing tip is advice on what to back
a top is a lid or cover

explanation.surface: Someone gives an excellent piece of advice on finding a better lid or covering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like the comparative of good, but it is someone who places bets, the person a tipster advises.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip-top is an informal adjective meaning first-rate or in perfect condition.

clue.text: Racehorse lacking a run will be unstable

indicators.note: the clue says the answer minus one letter is the wordplay word, so to build the answer that letter must be put back inside

parts.note: to totter is to wobble or be unsteady
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A horse that cannot run any more will become unsteady on its legs.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: take R out of TROTTER and you get TOTTER, which is what 'will be unstable' describes, so R goes back into TOTTER to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trotter is a horse bred and raced in harness at a trotting gait.

clue.text: Socialist knocks over fine drop of the hard stuff

indicators.note: knocking something over tips it upside down, which in a down entry turns the letters round

parts.note: OK means fine or all right
a nip is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: A left-winger downs a small glass of whisky in one go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocks over' reads as drinking quickly, but it turns the two pieces end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinko is a dismissive slang label for someone with left-wing or socialist leanings.

clue.text: He pours cocktail for brilliant classical musician

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bartender mixes a drink to honour a fine musician of the classical repertoire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classical' suggests Mozart or Haydn, but here it means Greek mythology.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Orpheus played the lyre so beautifully that he could charm animals, trees and even the gods of the underworld.

clue.text: Return theatre subsidy as a way to contain waste

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the letters run back the other way

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
aid is financial support or subsidy

explanation.surface: Someone argues that giving back an arts grant would cut wasteful spending.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'waste' sounds financial in the surface but is bodily waste; REPAID backwards also lurks in 'Return ... subsidy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Diaper is the American word for a nappy, an absorbent garment that holds a baby's urine and faeces.

clue.text: Without pressure, look into cricket perhaps

indicators.note: without means lacking, so one letter is taken away

parts.note: to inspect is to examine or look into
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Someone, freed from pressure, investigates the game of cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket here is the chirping creature, not the bat-and-ball game; 'perhaps' flags it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket is a jumping, chirping six-legged creature, one example of that class of animal.

clue.text: Power play — it's somewhat obvious!

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power
play in a rope or system is freedom of movement, i.e. latitude

explanation.surface: A cynic remarks that a political power play is rather transparent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power play' looks like one phrase but splits into the abbreviation and the slack sense of play.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitude is a trite remark so commonplace and predictable that it states what everyone already knows.

clue.text: Piece of old film on medical procedure put back in

parts.note: a reel is a spool holding a section of cine film
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy

explanation.surface: A fragment of archive footage about a hospital treatment gets spliced back in.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the first piece above the second. 'Put back in' sounds like editing film but means returning someone to office.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters who re-elect an official return that person to the post for another term.

clue.text: Assistant held up by aristocratic junior doctor

indicators.note: something held is gripped from both sides, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a patrician is a member of the nobility

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: A hospital helper is delayed by a posh trainee doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junior doctor' suggests a trainee; it means a doctor for juniors, i.e. children. 'Held up' reads as delayed, but splits into holding and turning upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A paediatrician is a medical specialist who treats children, playfully called juniors here.

clue.text: Unhappy as your solution won't fit like this!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: feeling low or depressed

definitions.text: your solution won't fit like this
definitions.meaning: second meaning: this is an across entry, so writing it vertically would not fit the grid

explanation.surface: A solver is miserable because their answer will not go into the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is self-referential: it talks about the grid itself, since this is an across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low is being blue or dejected, and the other direction in a grid is the vertical one.

clue.text: He's a dapper sort, although somewhat dumpy

indicators.note: to sort things is to arrange them, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A well-dressed man is described as smart, though a bit plump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort' reads as a noun meaning type of person, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear-shaped figure is broad at the hips and narrow at the top, so stocky or squat around the middle.

clue.text: Wise also to replace a fall guy

indicators.note: replacing means swapping one thing out and putting another in its place

parts.note: sage means wise
too means also
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clever person also takes over from someone set up to take the blame.
explanation.walkthrough: TOO goes where the A of SAGE was.
explanation.definitionFit: A stooge is a person used by others as a dupe or scapegoat, someone set up to take the blame.

clue.text: Conservative policy in document is rejected

indicators.note: something in another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the setter intends DEED, a legal document; only one E of it fits the grid
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a party line is its policy

explanation.surface: A Tory policy set out in an official paper gets voted down.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is faulty as published: the setter's legal document has two Es, which yields one letter too many, so solvers must ignore one E.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline an offer is to turn it down, so a declined proposal has been turned down or refused.

clue.text: One prepares chap at a wedding in America

definitions.text: One prepares chap at a wedding in America

parts.note: to groom is to get someone ready or smarten them
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A wedding attendant helps get the bridegroom ready for the ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer while its middle words build it; 'in America' signals the US term.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a groomsman is a male friend who attends the bridegroom, roughly a British usher or best man's helper.

clue.text: Having views about describing birds without wings?

parts.note: O is zero, the number of something you are without
pinions are wings, so a bird with wings could be called pinioned
surface padding framing the phrase as a description of birds

explanation.surface: Someone holds strong opinions on flightless birds.
explanation.walkthrough: A pinion is a bird's wing, so a bird with zero wings reads as O-pinioned; read normally, pinioned means wing-clipped, which also fits the flightless picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone opinioned holds firm beliefs, usually expressing them readily; it is a rarer form of opinionated.

clue.text: Gamble made by leading player using natural talent

indicators.note: leading things go at the front, so only the front letters of the following words count

parts.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A star performer takes a risk, relying on innate ability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading player' looks like the star of the show, but 'leading' governs all four following words.
explanation.definitionFit: To punt is British slang for placing a bet, and a punt is a wager on an uncertain outcome.

clue.text: Defeat flotilla occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A small fleet of ships is sometimes beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Take every other letter starting with the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To foil a plan is to thwart or prevent it from succeeding, a sense of beating it.

clue.text: Hide evidence of debts — that's mad

parts.note: fur is an animal's hide or pelt
IOUs are written acknowledgements of money owed

explanation.surface: Someone conceals their record of borrowing, which is crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' reads as a verb, conceal, but it is the noun for an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad here is the angry sense rather than insane, and furious means extremely angry.

clue.text: Artist providing tiny cream confection

indicators.note: a confection is something concocted from mixed ingredients, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter serves up a small creamy dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: Tracy Emin is a British artist, best known for My Bed, her unmade bed shown at the Tate.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracy Emin is a well-known contemporary British artist, so she is one example of a creative painter or sculptor.

clue.text: Mess left inside ship

indicators.note: something inside is enclosed, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a cutter is a small fast vessel
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Untidiness is left lying about below deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess' sounds naval, like a ship's dining room, but it is the untidiness sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Clutter is an untidy jumble of things lying about, a synonym for disorder or mess.

clue.text: Allow half-hearted duelling at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled
a heart that is only half there has lost part of its middle, so one central letter goes

parts.note: taken as written; its centre is a doubled letter

explanation.surface: Someone permits a feeble sword fight to take place on board ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of DUELLING is LL; removing half of it leaves DUELING to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To indulge someone is to let them have what they want, so it means to permit or humour.

clue.text: Live around loving couple? I don't care!

indicators.note: to go around something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
a couple in a relationship are said to be an item

explanation.surface: Someone asked to share a home with lovebirds shrugs dismissively.
explanation.walkthrough: Calling a couple 'an item' is informal slang for being romantically together.
explanation.definitionFit: Bite me is a rude slang retort expressing contempt or indifference, roughly whatever or get lost.

clue.text: American genius creates knock out current account

parts.note: to brain someone is to knock them out with a blow to the head
I is the physics symbol for electric current
AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A US prodigy produces a stunning version of a current affairs report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current account' looks like a bank account but splits in two; 'American' marks the word as US slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainiac is American slang for a highly intelligent person, a whiz or egghead.

clue.text: Resolving timeless dispute can be positive

indicators.note: resolving breaks something down and settles it anew, so the letters are rearranged
the suffix -less means lacking, so the word it is attached to stands for something removed

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Settling a never-ending quarrel can turn out well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' looks like everlasting, but it tells you to drop T from DISPUTE before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A positive, as a noun, is a good aspect or benefit, and so is the upside of a situation.

clue.text: Two short ways to create part of musical system

parts.note: St is short for Street, one kind of way
Ave is short for Avenue, another kind of way

explanation.surface: Two brief routes combine to form part of a music-notation scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: One fragment yields both pieces: two road abbreviations side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A stave, or staff, is the set of five horizontal lines on which notes are written in standard notation.

clue.text: Work to reduce effect of token performance

parts.note: a counter is a disc or token used in games
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: Someone tries to lessen the impact of a half-hearted show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Token performance' reads as a gesture made for show, but splits into two nouns.
explanation.definitionFit: To counteract something is to act against it so as to neutralise or offset its influence.

clue.text: Colleague right to leave mass meeting

indicators.note: something that leaves goes away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a rally is a large public gathering
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A co-worker wants to quit a big protest gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like an adjective about the colleague, but it is the single letter to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a partner or associate who supports you, much as a workmate or associate might.

clue.text: Study after turf becomes waterlogged

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf
a den is a private room for work, a study

explanation.surface: After rain, the lawn is soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the study second; 'Study' looks like a verb but is the room.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodden means soaked through and saturated, like ground full of rainwater.

clue.text: Don't move liberated zone that's been evacuated

parts.note: liberated means set free

indicators.note: an evacuated place has been emptied, so only its outer shell of letters remains

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Soldiers in a freed but deserted area are ordered to stay still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evacuated' is a common signal to empty a word of its insides.
explanation.definitionFit: Freeze is the command shouted to make someone stand completely still, as police do.
